mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 4% for two consecutive months reduces expected equity discount rates, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of FEDFUNDS > 4.0 regimes, or FEDFUNDS decline reverses before 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) coincides with stronger consumer demand, pushing S&P 500 20-day forward returns positively when labor conditions improve for two months.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 145,000 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite PAYEMS > 145,000 for 2 months, or other demand proxies (GDPC1) show contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp quarterly jump in GDPC1 (goods orders) followed by a monthly rise in HOUST (housing starts) predicts positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as it signals accelerating business and housing demand.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarter-on-quarter increase > 10% AND HOUST month-on-month increase > 5% in the same quarter
failure_condition: 60-day returns are flat or negative despite the combined signal, or GDPC1/HOUST show no correlation with SPX returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) below 105 for three months indicates supply-side softness, which is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO recovers above 105 before 20 days, or 20-day returns are positive despite the supply signal.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.5 percentage points in a single month, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is negative, reflecting risk aversion to rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increase > 0.5pp in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive during FEDFUNDS > +0.5pp months, or no significant effect detected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE (unemployment) below 4.5% for two consecutive months coincides with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates job market tightening.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative despite UNRATE < 4.5 for 2 months, or other labor proxies (PAYEMS) contradict the signal.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent monthly increases in GDPC1 and RSAFS (retail sales) above their 2021 Q4 averages for 4 weeks predict a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return via demand acceleration.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 16500 AND RSAFS > 460,000 for 4 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: 20-day returns flat or negative despite the combined demand signal, or proxies show no correlation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL (CPI) of over 0.3% for three months suggests persistent inflation pressures, which is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns positive during CPIAUCSL declines, or CPIAUCSL stabilizes before the horizon.
